tagline: Two villages on an old stagecoach line.
intro: From Waynesville, where the Little Miami River runs through town, the byway follows the early nineteenth-century Accommodation stagecoach line about 11.6 miles to Spring Valley. Historic farms lie along the way, with a historic district at either end.

Waynesville was laid out in 1796 and built up chiefly by Quakers; since 1970 it has held a fall Sauerkraut Festival. Off the road, the Little Miami Scenic Trail runs 63 paved miles beside the river for walkers, cyclists and riders on horseback.

moments.title: Waynesville Main Street
moments.text: The historic district runs about five blocks along Main Street, from just below South Street to Franklin Road, and takes in the 1844 Waynesville Academy.

moments.title: Waynesville Engine House and Lockup
moments.text: Built in 1881 as the village's first fire station, the engine house got a fire truck in 1886 and, the same year, a jail added at the back.

moments.title: Spring Valley
moments.text: The village began with the arrival of the Little Miami Railroad and was platted in 1844.
